The United States moved to force TikTok’s divestiture or ban due to national security concerns, specifically the risk of Chinese government access to US user data and its recommendation algorithm [Source: ev-1]. This concern was formalized in legislation signed by President Biden on 2024-04-24, which required ByteDance to divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by an additional 90 days) or face a ban [Source: ev-1]. The Supreme Court upheld this law with a unanimous 9-0 decision on 2025-01-17, one day before the effective date of 2025-0-19 [Source: ev-1].

The dispute was resolved through a negotiated deal rather than an outright sale. Following a brief service outage in the US from 2025-18/19 that lasted roughly 14 hours, President Trump pledged to pause enforcement and issued an executive order on 2025--01-20 delaying it for 75 days [Source: ev-1]. The final resolution, announced per Bloomberg on 202-6-10, established TikTok's US operations as a joint venture where ByteDance retained majority interest, but Oracle received approximately a 12.5% stake along with other investors like SoftBank [Source: ev-1]. This structure included "Project Texas," which involved hosting US user data in Oracle's cloud under US control [Source: ev-1].
